findings.title: Punishment is feared as a change of allegiance
findings.claim: The warning makes the feared harm consequential not only as pain that reaches the father but as entry into a supporting relation with Satan, away from the mercy named as its source.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers أَخَافُ, يَمَسَّكَ, عَذَابٌ, and وَلِيًّا respectively frame the forecast, the reaching effect, the punitive event, and the resulting relation. The wider warning at 11:26, punitive-touch wording at 21:46 and 6:49, and explicit Satan-as-walī wording at 4:119 supply independent contacts, changing the reading from an isolated threat into a relational consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning's seriousness becomes perceptible as the risk of being drawn into the wrong protecting or supporting relation, not only of suffering pain.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains a filial warning about punishment and Satanic allegiance. This does not claim that عذاب lexically means allegiance, that touch is non-physical, or that target-side morphology beyond the supplied Arabic is established.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and the published support are trusted and exact; global target rows provide exact Arabic and connection notes but omit target morphology, so the wider recurrence is qualified rather than treated as a complete lexical proof.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir belirtiye dayanarak kötü bir şey bekleme korkusu
branch_activations.facet_statement: İstenmeyen bir olayın gerçekleşeceği, bilinen ya da sanılan bir belirtiye dayanılarak beklenir.
branch_activations.carrier: أَخَافُ carries the speaker's apprehensive expectation of an unwanted event.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 11:26 places a messenger's fear beside false worship and a painful day of punishment.
branch_activations.activation: The independent pairing of fear, false worship, and punishment gives the focus fear-word a concrete warning trigger and confirms that its object is a projected consequence, while the focus adds the filial addressee.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speaker's fear is a protective forecast of a moral consequence, not an undirected emotional reaction.
branch_activations.boundary: The 11:26 parallel does not establish the target's morphology beyond its supplied Arabic and does not replace the focus's own father-directed scene.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiye ağır acı verilir veya ağır bir ceza uygulanır.
branch_activations.carrier: عَذَابٌ names the punitive event feared for the father.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 21:46 describes even a touch of the Lord's punishment reaching wrongdoers and producing confession.
branch_activations.activation: The independent image of a small punitive touch meeting its moral consequence makes the focus's عَذَابٌ a concrete, reaching punishment rather than an abstract threat.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared event is an inflicted punitive consequence whose contact can expose the addressee's condition.
branch_activations.boundary: This retains punishment as the focus sense; it does not set a scale for the punishment or infer target-side morphology not supplied in the packet.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: iyi ya da kötü bir etkiye uğrama
branch_activations.facet_statement: İyi ya da kötü bir etki kişiye veya onun malına erişir ve onda bir iz bırakır.
branch_activations.carrier: يَمَسَّكَ carries the event of an effect reaching the father.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 6:49 says that punishment touches those who deny the signs because of their transgression.
branch_activations.activation: The independent touch-punishment construction gives the focus contact verb an effect-bearing use: the harm reaches a person and leaves a consequential mark, while the focus places that contact inside the father's feared future.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared touch is an impact that changes the person's condition, not merely a physical contact image.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch includes a wider good-or-bad effect, but this finding retains only the negative realization licensed by the focus and does not erase the ordinary touch sense.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sevgi, dostluk, inanç veya yardım bağıyla birinin yanında yer alma.
branch_activations.carrier: وَلِيًّا assigns the father a resulting role of standing with and supporting Satan.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 4:119 explicitly describes taking Satan as a walī instead of God and calls the result manifest loss.
branch_activations.activation: The independent Satan-walī construction returns through the focus predicate and makes the feared state a chosen support or allegiance relation rather than a mere encounter with Satan.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The warning reaches a change of relational side: the father could become a supporter of the adversarial power.
branch_activations.boundary: The target's broader loss judgment is not imported, and this does not claim that every walī use has the Satan-directed sense.

findings.title: Punishment is also heard as loss of mercy's nearness
findings.claim: The punishment named as coming from al-Rahman can also be perceived as the loss of mercy's protective nearness: the Satan-name supplies distance from that source, while a wider mercy text makes withholding a real relational consequence.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers رَّحْمَٰنِ, الشَّيْطَانِ, and عَذَابٌ meet wider contacts where mercy and punishment are paired, remembrance of al-Rahman is abandoned before a Satanic companion is assigned, and mercy is explicitly opened or withheld. That contact lets the supplied deprivation reading deepen the punitive warning without changing its grammatical subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The danger becomes perceptible as loss of relational shelter and benevolent reach, not only as pain imposed from outside.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains a warning that punishment may touch the father and that he may become Satan's walī. This does not claim that عذاب lexically means withholding, that الشَّيْطَانِ literally denotes physical distance here, or that the weaker cross-run grade is a settled lexical conclusion.

epistemic.reason: The published support is trusted but carries an embedded weak grade; the focus branches are explicit and the global contacts are concrete, while target morphology is not supplied, so the deprivation relation remains qualified.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: الرَّحْمَٰنِ names the divine source whose mercy and benevolent reach frame the feared punishment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 17:54 places divine mercy and divine punishment together under God's knowledge and will.
branch_activations.activation: The independent mercy-punishment pairing meets the focus source preposition and mercy-name, making the punishment's relation to mercy perceptible rather than leaving the name as a detached title.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared punishment can be heard against the loss or withdrawal of the Merciful's benevolent reach while still remaining punishment.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not state that mercy has been withdrawn, and this activation does not infer a target-side lexical analysis beyond the supplied Arabic.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel anlam, bir şeyin uzakta bulunması ya da bulunduğu yerden uzaklaşmasıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: الشَّيْطَانِ carries the packet's distance-and-removal pressure within the named adversarial relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 43:36 describes turning away from the remembrance of al-Rahman before a Satanic companion is assigned.
branch_activations.activation: The wider movement away from al-Rahman's remembrance gives the focus Satan-name an independent relational-distance trigger, while the assigned companion supplies the contrasting proximity that the focus fears.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Satanic nearness can be perceived as the other side of distance from mercy, so the feared walī state marks a trajectory of alienation as well as affiliation.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a relational resonance, not a claim that the proper name is being used as a literal physical-distance noun or that the target morphology is established.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi başkasını bir işten uzak tutar veya o işi ona bıraktırır.
branch_activations.carrier: عَذَابٌ remains the noun naming the feared punitive event, now under a bounded withholding-of-mercy pressure.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 35:2 explicitly describes mercy being opened and withheld, with no one able to release what God withholds.
branch_activations.activation: The independent withholding relation gives the punishment carrier a deprivation contact: the focus's punishment from al-Rahman can be heard alongside mercy no longer reaching the person, without converting the noun into a different grammatical role.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared punishment includes the possibility of being kept outside the Merciful's benevolent reach alongside the ordinary punitive consequence.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a global contextual resonance, not a lexical synonym for withholding, not an assertion that عذاب is a hidden agent, and not an exclusion of inflicted punishment.

findings.title: Allegiance exposes a governing power
findings.claim: Through the focus form وَلِيًّا, the feared Satanic relation can also be perceived as subjection to an authority, not merely friendly proximity.
findings.mechanism: The focus predicate وَلِيًّا carries the branch facet of undertaking and managing another's condition, while the independent 16:100 connection states that Satan's authority is over those who take him as walī. Their contact changes the result clause from a static association into a relation that can govern the person's direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The feared allegiance becomes active dependence on a power that directs the person's condition, making the warning more than a label for companionship.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains that the father may become Satan's walī. This finding does not claim that every walī use means governance, nor does it import target morphology or a complete doctrine of authority.

epistemic.reason: An exact focus branch and exact target Arabic support the relation, but the connection's strong prior label is a review nomination rather than a source-trust field and the target morphology is absent.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir işi veya başkasının durumunu üstlenip yönetme ve yürütme.
branch_activations.carrier: وَلِيًّا names the predicate relation assigned to the father.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 16:100 says that Satan's authority is over those who take him as walī and associate others with God.
branch_activations.activation: The wider authority statement meets the focus's walī predicate and supplies the independent governing dimension of the relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Becoming Satan's walī can be heard as coming under an active authority that manages the person's course, not only as standing near an ally.
branch_activations.boundary: The target's authority statement is not used to claim that the focus grammatically names a formal office or that governance is the only walī sense.

findings.title: The feared alliance can divert its companion
findings.claim: Through the focus form الشَّيْطَانِ, the feared walī relation can also be perceived as a force that turns its companions away from the path while leaving them convinced they are guided.
findings.mechanism: The focus's named Satan carries the available direction-separation branch, and the independent 43:37 connection explicitly describes devils barring their companions from the path while those companions suppose themselves guided. The contact changes Satanic allegiance from a static association into an active redirection.
findings.reader_payoff: The danger of the relation becomes visible as loss of direction under the appearance of guidance.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains the warning against becoming Satan's walī. This does not claim that the focus itself contains the word path, that every Satan reference activates diversion, or that target-side morphology is supplied.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and target Arabic provide a concrete return, but the connection's strong prior label is only a review nomination and the target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yönünden ayırma ve bağlama göre eğrilik ya da çetinlik
branch_activations.facet_statement: Yalın eylem, bir kişiyi niyet ettiği yön ve doğrultudan ayırmayı ya da ona ters düşmeyi anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: الشَّيْطَانِ carries the named adversarial presence that the focus fears becoming aligned with.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 43:37 says that devils turn their companions away from the path while the companions think they are guided.
branch_activations.activation: The independent diversion-and-apparent-guidance relation meets the focus Satan carrier and activates the branch's direction-separation facet.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared Satanic alliance can be understood as active removal from an intended direction under a false sense of guidance.
branch_activations.boundary: This is not a lexical claim that الشَّيْطَانِ means path-diversion in every use, and it does not import missing target morphology.
